title: Rulebook Harmonizer and Regional-Tier Compatibility Checker
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: The current routing rule runtime accepts a permissive JSON/YAML DSL that has grown ad-hoc: region selectors, tier constraints, and fallback model variants live in different shapes. This leads to brittle rollouts, surprising fallbacks, and hard-to-reason migration paths when we introduce new variant types (eg. quantized variants, ondemand vs reserved).

Goal: Replace the ad-hoc checks with a rigorous, typed validation and transformation pipeline that: 1) validates new rule schemas at intake (CLI/Console/API), 2) provides clear, actionable lint messages and autofixes where safe, 3) emits a stable typed IR for the runtime to consume, and 4) includes a compatibility shim so older deployments continue working during staged migration.

Scope: Schema design + validator + linter + compatibility adapter + CI gating + unit/integration tests. Does NOT include the runtime execution engine changes beyond consuming the new IR (separate followup).
acceptance_criteria: A typed schema (OpenAPI + JSON Schema annotations) exists that models: region selectors, tier weights/priorities, fallback model variants (family, quantization, capacity-tier), and policy predicates (customer-tier, latency-SLO, region-blocklist)
A validator that runs in the policy intake path (Console/API/CLI) and in CI, producing machine-readable errors and human-friendly lints
A backward-compatible compatibility adapter that can load legacy rules and emit the typed IR with documented transformation rules

End-to-end integration test demonstrating: a) canary route with region affinity, b) tiered routing between reserved and ondemand capacity, c) fallback to compatible model variant when primary variant is unavailable
No change in tenant-facing API surface for at least one release during migration; customers can opt-in to strict mode
Performance overhead of validation < 5ms per rule in the common case (cached schema/IR path)
technical_notes: Prefer a small typed AST (Rust/TypeScript) for the IR rather than raw JSON during runtime to avoid schema recursion and ambiguous semantics
Validation will be implemented as two layers: syntactic (JSON Schema) + semantic (typed rule checks: weight sums, exclusivity constraints, region overlap detection)
Implement autofix hints for common issues (eg. missing default fallback, sum-of-weights != 1) and integrate with Console UX to propose fixes

Compatibility shim strategy: add a translation layer that maps legacy keys (region_preference -> primary_affinity) and normalizes variant naming (eg. model: 'm-1' -> family: 'm', variant_hint: 'm-1.quant')
Plan to expose a diagnostic mode producing a deterministic hash of the typed IR for rollout safety checks and to power unit test assertions
Keep validator language-agnostic: core rules in OpenAPI/JSONSchema + reference implementation in TypeScript; later port to Rust for embedding in runtime if needed
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Introduce validator as opt-in flag (--strict-schema) and Console preview for orgs on staging. Phase 2: Run validator in CI for all policy changes and surface lint errors as warnings for one release. Phase 3: Enable strict mode by default and begin serving typed IR to runtime with compatibility adapter enabled. Final Phase: Deprecate legacy keys (announce 3 release window).
test_plan: Unit tests for JSON Schema and semantic checks. Integration tests using local runtime harness: simulate region loss and verify fallback variant chosen per policy. Fuzzing: feed randomized legacy shapes through adapter and assert deterministic IR and no runtime exceptions. Add end-to-end test in runner CI that creates a routing policy, deploys a canary, and verifies traffic split and fallback behavior.
notes_and_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff sync with PM (A. Patel) and Design (Maya Chen). Agreed on primary invariants: deterministic fallback path, explicit default variant required unless global default exists.
2026-02-18: PoC validator prototype (TS) that rejects rules missing fallback; initial lint messages reviewed by Console UX. Feedback: provide autofix suggestion rather than blocking in strict mode.
2026-02-25: Security review flagged KMS policy inclusion when rules reference per-tenant encrypted variant metadata — added to dependencies for Private deploy checklist.

2026-03-02: Engineering review: decided to use JSON Schema draft-07 for syntactic checks and a separate TS semantic layer to keep error messages actionable. Nick (runtime) requested typed IR minor shape change to include 'variant_compatibility_tags' for fast runtime matching.

2026-03-05: Implemented compatibility adapter v0.2; demoed to infra; PR #482 opened for early feedback. Benchmarked validation time: cold 12ms, warm (cached) 1.8ms — aligns with target after optimizing schema compilation.
